summary: Depth is caller leverage, not code volume; retain the glossary and alternative designs while making costs and reference-only scope explicit.

supporting_disposition.reason: Retain four dependency categories and interface tests; replace blanket test deletion with demonstrated coverage substitution.
Retain contrasting design constraints and caller examples while supporting available concurrency and bounded design scope.
Preserve source UI metadata and invocation policy exactly.
Retain Matt Pocock MIT attribution in every refactored package.

deltas.change: Make reference-only behavior explicit and scope alternative design to the selected module.
deltas.reason: A glossary should not authorize a redesign campaign.
deltas.tradeoff: The user or driver must actually select a design problem.

deltas.change: Keep defined vocabulary but permit exact project and technology terms.
deltas.reason: Calling an HTTP API an API or a deployed service a service need not obscure module reasoning.

deltas.change: Evaluate total caller obligations, not method count alone.
deltas.reason: One method with modes, sequencing, and hidden errors may be a huge interface.
deltas.tradeoff: Depth remains a judgment rather than a numeric score.

deltas.change: Treat second-adapter and public-test heuristics as evidence, not universal laws.
deltas.reason: Policy boundaries and localized diagnostic tests can be justified independently.

deltas.change: Replace shallow tests only after verifying that new tests preserve meaningful coverage.
deltas.reason: Interface tests need not cover every old invariant automatically.
deltas.tradeoff: A temporary overlap may remain during migration.
